main_result: The manuscript claims Thompson's group F is not amenable (Theorem 1.1, "thm:main"). It is presented as resolving Geoghegan's conjecture. It also states two corollaries, on uniformly bounded non-unitarizable representations and on Bernoulli percolation on Cayley graphs of F, both derived from unpublished companion papers by the same authors.
proof_strategy: Assume F is amenable, so Følner sets A exist for a fixed finite set S of transports (Section 2.3, Lemma dyad:transport). Build a recursive Hilbert-ball-valued coloring of basic dyadic partitions, p(T) = f(mean of p(T_{I_j})), with f a fixed-point-free Lipschitz self-map of the unit ball with uniform displacement delta (Lemma displacement, proved explicitly in Appendix A). Covariance of normalized restrictions under transports (eq. dyad:covariance) makes scalar correlations of separated parent/child colors agree with one common value alpha up to eta = max_{h in S} |hA Δ A|/|A| (eq. avg:correlation). Averaging the identity X_{I_i} = f(z_i) over A and expanding squared norms gives E||z_i - m||^2 <= 4/D + 4(1-1/D) eta, and then delta^2 <= L^2(4/D + 4(1-1/D) eta). For D > 4L^2/delta^2 and small eta this is a contradiction with Følner sets. I checked the algebra of each variance and mixed-term bound, the covariance identity, admissibility of hg for g in A, and the appendix's speed, tangent, nonvanishing and displacement estimates; I did not find a step I could refute. The corollaries are not verifiable from the text.
hardest_part: The argument is short, and every step I checked holds. That makes the claim unusually strong: a few pages would settle a long-standing open problem. I could not rule out a subtle error in the global logic (for example, in how the single level n, chosen per A, interacts with the fixed S and the parent/child interval family), and I cannot independently confirm novelty or the cited literature. The appendix's Lipschitz bookkeeping for G (Proposition aux:map) was the least fully checked piece: I verified its constants, but the 'product estimates' step is stated rather than shown.

main_result: Claims that Thompson's group F is not amenable (Theorem 1.1). The argument: take a fixed-point-free Lipschitz self-map f of the Hilbert ball with ||f(x)-x|| >= delta. Build recursive colorings of dyadic partitions, one for each group element, so that at a sufficiently fine level the colors of nested and separated intervals satisfy scalar-correlation identities. Averaging over a finite A, the correlation defects are bounded by the Folner defect eta(A) = max_{h in S} |hA Delta A|/|A| for a fixed finite S. Then Proposition 3.2 gives eta(A) >= c0 > 0 for every finite nonempty A, contradicting the Folner criterion. Corollaries 4.1 and 4.2 are consequences via cited companion results.
proof_strategy: Section 2 proves dyadic bookkeeping: normalized restrictions, the covariance identity (hg T)_{I'} = (gT)_I for an affine transport h, and that finitely many group elements are admissible at a common fine level. Section 2.2 defines colors p(T) recursively via f and a parent family I_1<...<I_D with D > 4L^2/delta^2. Proposition 3.2 compares averaged correlations of separated intervals to a common value alpha (error eta, via finite-translation cancellation over hA cap A). It then bounds E_A||z_i - m||^2 by 4/D + 4(1-1/D)eta using expansion and sign bounds on diagonal, nested and separated pairs. Combining with ||m - f(m)||^2 <= (L^2/D) sum ||z_i - m||^2 and ||m-f(m)|| >= delta gives the uniform bound. The appendix constructs f explicitly on L^2([0,1];R^2) via a tube about a curve gamma with unit speed bounded below, orthogonal rotations R_t, and G(x)=x+beta q v + chi(R_t-I)e, with f = -G/||G||. I checked the algebra of the variance and mixed-term estimates, the covariance identity, the tube and injectivity estimates, and the nonvanishing and Lipschitz bounds for G; I found no definite error. Remaining uncertainty is in terse steps and in the cited companion results.
hardest_part: The hardest part to certify is the combined bookkeeping in Section 3: admissibility at a single level n that depends on A, the covariance identity used to equate X_I(g) with X_{I_1}(h_{I,J}g), and the resulting uniform defect eta. Each piece checks out on its own, but the argument settles a long-open problem with a short proof, so I would not trust my reading as a full verification. The appendix Lipschitz estimates for G (a long product-rule argument stated only as "one finite Lipschitz bound") are the other place I could not fully redo the constants quickly.

main_result: The manuscript claims Thompson's group F is not amenable. Its argument: for each finite A in F, some transport h in a fixed finite set S satisfies |hA Δ A|/|A| >= (δ²/L² - 4/D)/(4(1-1/D)) > 0, which contradicts Følner's condition for S. The appendix gives a Hilbert-space Lipschitz map f: B -> B with ||f(x)-x|| >= 1/2. Corollaries on uniformly bounded non-unitarizable representations and on Bernoulli percolation are deduced from the nonamenability via cited companion results.
proof_strategy: The author builds a recursive coloring p of dyadic partitions with values in the unit ball, via p(T) = f(average of p(T_{I_j})) when T respects the parent intervals I_j. Group elements g are colored by X_I(g) = p((gT^(n))_I), so transports h in S give X_I(g) = X_{I_1}(hg), and every separated pair of colored intervals has average inner product within η of one common α. Using X_{I_i} = f(z_i) and the Lipschitz displacement bound on the mean m, the author bounds E||z_i - m||² by 4/D + 4(1-1/D)η, so the displacement δ² is at most L²(4/D + 4η) on average over A. Choosing D large contradicts small η, giving the Følner violation. I checked the arithmetic of the variance and mixed-term estimates, the covariance identity, and the appendix nonvanishing and normalization estimates; I could not find an algebraic error in them.
hardest_part: Proposition avg:boundary: whether a single level n, a single α, and the transports in S simultaneously make every separated correlation within η of α, uniformly over all pairs (parents and descendants). I checked the covariance and admissibility chain, but the argument is short for a conjecture open since 1979, and I cannot rule out a subtle failure in the cross-pair bookkeeping. I also could not identify which specific property of F the argument uses beyond dyadic transport, which makes it hard to test the argument against amenable groups.
